question: What is a reason to create a formula when ingesting a data stream?
optionA: To concatenate files so they are ingested in the correct sequence
optionB: To add a unique external identifier to an existing ruleset
optionC: To transform a date-time field into a date field for use in data mapping
optionD: To remove duplicate rows of data from the data stream
explanation:
Formula fields in data stream ingestion are used to derive new values from existing fields at the point of ingestion. Converting a datetime field into a plain date field is a classic use case — it produces a new field that can then be cleanly mapped to a DMO attribute. Concatenating ingestion sequences (A), adding external identifiers to rulesets (B), and deduplication (D) are not functions of formula fields.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_batch_transform_formula.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_considerations_formula_fields.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: A consultant wants to build a new audience in Data Cloud. Which three criteria can the consultant include when building a segment? (Choose 3)
optionA: Direct attributes
optionB: Data stream attributes
optionC: Calculated Insights
optionD: Related attributes
explanation:
When building a segment in Data Cloud the available filter criteria are: Direct attributes (fields directly on the segmented DMO), Related attributes (fields reachable via DMO relationships), and Calculated Insights (pre-computed metrics or dimensions). Data stream attributes (B) cannot be used directly in segmentation — data must first be mapped to a DMO. Streaming insights (E) are near-real-time aggregations used for data actions, not segment criteria.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_insights.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_calculated_insights_in_segments.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Northern Trail Outfitters (NTO) is configuring an identity resolution ruleset based on Fuzzy Name and Normalized Email. What should NTO do to ensure the best email address is activated?
optionA: Include Contact Point Email object Is Active field as a match rule
optionB: Use the source priority order in activations to make sure a contact point from the desired source is delivered to the activation target
optionC: Ensure Marketing Cloud is prioritized as the first data source in the Source Priority reconciliation rule
optionD: Set the default reconciliation rule to Last Updated
explanation:
Reconciliation rules determine which field value wins on the unified profile, but the contact point that is actually sent in an activation is governed by the source priority order configured on the activation itself. By ordering preferred sources first, NTO ensures the highest-quality email address is delivered to the target. Making a field a match rule (A) affects identity resolution, not which contact point is activated. Setting Source Priority only on the ruleset (C) controls the unified profile attribute, not the activated contact point. Last Updated (D) reconciliation applies to profile attributes, not to selecting the best email for activation.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_contact_points.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: A consultant is preparing to implement Data Cloud. Which ethic should the consultant adhere to regarding customer data?
optionA: Allow senior leaders in the firm to access customer data for audit purposes
optionB: Collect and use all of the data to create more personalized experiences
optionC: Map sensitive data to the same DMO for ease of deletion
optionD: Carefully consider asking for sensitive data such as age, gender, or ethnicity
explanation:
Data ethics in Data Cloud implementations requires consultants to apply data minimization and proportionality — only collect data that is necessary and appropriate. Sensitive attributes like age, gender, and ethnicity carry heightened privacy risk and regulatory obligations (GDPR, CCPA), so their collection should be carefully justified. Broad collection of all available data (B) violates minimization principles. Granting leadership access for audits (A) requires proper controls, not blanket access. Grouping sensitive data in one DMO (C) is an operational concern, not an ethical principle.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_consent_management.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Which statement about Data Cloud's Web and Mobile Application Connector is true?
optionA: A standard schema containing event, profile, and transaction data is created at the time the connector is configured
optionB: The Tenant Specific Endpoint is auto-generated in Data Cloud when setting the connector
optionC: Any data streams associated with the connector will be automatically deleted upon deleting the app from Data Cloud Setup
optionD: The connector schema can be updated to delete an existing field
explanation:
When configuring the Web and Mobile Application Connector, Data Cloud automatically generates a Tenant Specific Endpoint URL that the SDK uses to send events. No standard schema is pre-created (A) — the schema is defined based on what the developer instruments. Deleting the app from setup does not cascade-delete data streams (C). Fields on a connector schema cannot be deleted once created (D) — only new fields can be added.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_web_mobile_app_connector.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Northern Trail Outfitters unifies individuals in its Data Cloud instance. Which three features can a consultant use to validate the data on a unified profile? (Choose 3)
optionA: Identity Resolution
optionB: Query APL
optionC: Data Explorer
optionD: Profile Explorer
explanation:
To validate data on a unified profile, consultants use: Identity Resolution (A) — review match and reconciliation statistics and run the ruleset; Data Explorer (C) — inspect rows in any DLO or DMO; and Profile Explorer (D) — look up a specific unified individual and see all their linked source records and contact points. Query APL (B) is for querying data but not purpose-built for profile validation. Data Actions (E) trigger downstream events and are not validation tools.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_data_explorer.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_profile_explorer.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_identity_resolution.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: A consultant is connecting sales order data to Data Cloud and considers whether to use the Profile, Engagement, or Other categories to map the DLO. The consultant chooses to map the DLO called Order-Headers to the Sales Order DMO using the Engagement category. What is the impact of this action on future mappings?
optionA: A DLO with category Engagement can be mapped to any DMO using either Profile, Engagement, or Other categories
optionB: When mapping a Profile DLO to the Sales Order DMO, the category gets updated to Profile
optionC: Sales Order DMO gets assigned to both the Profile and Engagement categories when mapping a Profile DLO
optionD: Only Engagement category DLOs can be mapped to the Sales Order DMO. Sales Order gets assigned to the Engagement Category
explanation:
Category is chosen on the data stream, and Salesforce is explicit that you can't change it after the data stream is saved. The category also pins the target DMO: a DMO's category is set when the DMO is created and can't be changed afterwards, so once Order-Headers is mapped to Sales Order under Engagement, Sales Order is an Engagement-category DMO and only Engagement DLOs can map to it thereafter (D). The category does not flip to Profile on a later mapping (B), does not accumulate both categories (C), and is not freely interchangeable (A). The practical consequence shows up in the mapping requirements, which differ by category: Profile and Other DMOs require the primary key to be mapped before the mapping can be saved, while Engagement DMOs require both the primary key and an event date-time field.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_category.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_required_data_mappings.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_map_custom_data_model_objects.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: The leadership team at Cumulus Financial has determined that customers who deposited more than $250,000 in the last five years and are not using advisory services will be the central focus for all new campaigns in the next year. Which features support this use case?
optionA: Calculated insight and data action
optionB: Calculated insight and segment
optionC: Streaming insight and segment
optionD: Streaming insight and data action
explanation:
This use case requires aggregating historical deposit totals over five years and filtering on advisory service usage — both are batch analytical computations, making Calculated Insights the right tool. The resulting metric is then used to build a segment that targets those customers for campaigns. Streaming insights (C, D) work on near-real-time windows, not multi-year historical aggregations. A data action (A, D) triggers an event for individual records, not a batch audience for campaigns.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_insights.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_calculated_insights_in_segments.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Northern Trail Outfitters (NTO) is getting ready to start ingesting its CRM data into Data Cloud. While setting up the connector, which type of refresh should NTO expect when the data stream is deployed for the first time?
optionA: Incremental
optionB: Manual refresh
optionC: Partial refresh
optionD: Full refresh
explanation:
The first deployment of a CRM Connector data stream always performs a Full refresh to load all existing records from the Salesforce org into Data Cloud. Subsequent runs use incremental refreshes to sync only changed records. Manual refresh (B) is a user-triggered action available after initial deployment. Partial refresh (C) is not a standard Data Cloud refresh type.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_salesforce_crm_connector.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_data_stream_schedule.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=000389693&language=en_US&type=1

question: If a data source does not have a field that can be designated as a primary key, what should the consultant do?
optionA: Use the default primary key recommended by Data Cloud
optionB: Create a composite key by combining two or more source fields through a formula field
optionC: Select a field as a primary key and then add a key qualifier
optionD: Remove duplicates from the data source and then select a primary key
explanation:
When no single field can serve as a unique primary key, the correct approach is to create a composite key using a formula field that concatenates two or more source fields that together produce a unique value. Data Cloud does not auto-generate a default primary key (A). A key qualifier is used alongside an existing primary key, not as a substitute for one (C). Removing duplicates (D) is a data quality step but does not create a key where none exists.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_primary_key.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: A consultant wants to ensure that every segment managed by multiple brand teams adheres to the same set of exclusion criteria, that are updated on a monthly basis. What is the most efficient option to allow for this capability?
optionA: Create, publish, and deploy a data kit
optionB: Create a reusable container block with common criteria
optionC: Create a nested segment
optionD: Create a segment and copy it for each brand
explanation:
Salesforce's documented mechanism for sharing criteria across segments is the nested segment: its help page opens with "Reuse filters and maintain consistency in your data by using an existing segment built on profile objects to build a new nested segment." Build the monthly exclusion criteria once as a segment, nest it inside each brand team's segment, and the monthly update is made in one place. A container is a different thing entirely — it is created automatically on the segment canvas when you filter on a related attribute, it scopes those attributes to the same data row of the container's DMO, and it belongs to the segment it sits in. Containers are not shareable or reusable across segments, so there is no reusable container block to maintain. A data kit (A) packages configuration for deployment between orgs rather than sharing logic within one, and copying a segment per brand (D) is exactly the duplication the requirement is trying to avoid.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_nested_segments.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.c360_a_container_basics.htm&language=en_US&type=5

corrected.note: Answer moved B->C. The keyed reusable container block is not a Data Cloud feature: a container is auto-created for related-attribute filters and is scoped to its own segment. Nested segments are what the documentation names for reusing filters and maintaining consistency, and the old explanation dismissed that correct option as less efficient.

question: A customer has outlined requirements to trigger a journey for an abandoned browse behavior. Based on the requirements, the consultant determines they will use streaming insights to trigger a data action to Journey Builder every hour. How should the consultant configure the solution to ensure the data action is triggered at the cadence required?
optionA: Set the activation schedule to hourly
optionB: Configure the data to be ingested in hourly batches
optionC: Set the journey entry schedule to run every hour
optionD: Set the insights aggregation time window to 1 hour
explanation:
Streaming insights use an aggregation time window to define how often the insight is computed and evaluated. Setting the aggregation time window to 1 hour causes the insight — and any associated data action — to fire every hour based on the rolling window of streaming data. The activation schedule (A) controls segment-based activations, not data actions from streaming insights. Ingestion batch frequency (B) affects when data arrives, not when the action fires. The Journey entry schedule (C) controls entry into the Journey independently of Data Cloud's trigger cadence.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_insights.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: A customer has two Data Cloud orgs. A new configuration has been completed and tested for an Amazon S3 data stream and its mappings in one of the Data Cloud orgs. What is recommended to package and promote this configuration to the customer's second org?
optionA: Use the Metadata API
optionB: Use the Salesforce CRM connector
optionC: Create a data kit
optionD: Package as an AppExchange application
explanation:
Data kits are the native Data Cloud mechanism for packaging and deploying configurations — including data streams, mappings, and other metadata — from one Data Cloud org to another. They are purpose-built for this promotion pattern. The Metadata API (A) does not support Data Cloud-specific metadata types. The CRM Connector (B) is for ingesting Salesforce CRM data, not for configuration migration. AppExchange packaging (D) is an ISV distribution model, not a deployment pattern for customer orgs.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_data_package_kits.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: A consultant is integrating an Amazon S3 activated campaign with the customer's destination system. In order for the destination system to find the metadata about the segment, which file on the S3 will contain this information for processing?
optionA: The .txt file
optionB: The .json file
optionC: The .csv file
optionD: The .zip file
explanation:
When Data Cloud activates to Amazon S3, two files are written: a .csv file containing the actual data payload (the segment members and their attributes), and a .json manifest file containing metadata about the segment — such as segment name, activation ID, run timestamp, and schema details. The destination system reads the .json file to understand the structure and context of the activation before processing the .csv.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_find_segments_in_cloud_file_storage.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Northern Trail Outfitters (NTO) owns and operates six unique brands, each with their own set of customers, transactions, and loyalty information. The marketing director wants to ensure that segments and activations from the NTO Outlet brand do not reference customers or transactions from the other brands. What is the most efficient approach to handle this requirement?
optionA: Use Business Unit Aware activation
optionB: Separate the Outlet brand into a data space
optionC: Separate the brands into six different data spaces
optionD: Create a batch data transform to generate a DLO for the Outlet brand
explanation:
Data spaces provide logical partitions within a single Data Cloud org, ensuring that segments and activations only reference data within that space. Isolating just the Outlet brand into its own data space efficiently enforces the separation requirement without the overhead of six separate spaces (C). Business Unit Aware activation (A) applies to Marketing Cloud BUs, not to data isolation within Data Cloud. A batch data transform (D) creates a new DLO but does not enforce segmentation boundaries.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_data_spaces.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Northern Trail Outfitters asks its consultant to extract the runner profiles and activity logs from its Track My Run mobile app and load them into Data Cloud. The marketing department also indicates that they need the last 90 days of historical data and want all new and updated data as it becomes available on a go-forward basis. As best practice, which sequence of actions should the consultant use to implement this request?
optionA: Use bulk ingestion to first load the last 90 days of data, and also subsequently use bulk ingestion to synchronize the future data as it becomes available
optionB: Use streaming ingestion to first load the last 90 days of data, and also subsequently use streaming ingestion to synchronize future data as it becomes available
optionC: Use streaming ingestion to first load the last 90 days of data, and then use bulk ingestion to synchronize future data as it becomes available
optionD: Use bulk ingestion to first load the last 90 days of data, and then use streaming ingestion to synchronize future data as it becomes available
explanation:
The best-practice pattern for this scenario is to use bulk (batch) ingestion for the initial historical backfill — it is designed for large volumes of historical data — and then switch to streaming ingestion for ongoing near-real-time updates as new activity logs arrive. Streaming ingestion is not suited for large historical loads (B, C). Using bulk for ongoing sync (A) introduces latency that conflicts with the 'as it becomes available' requirement.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_data_ingestion.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_data_stream_schedule.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Data Cloud receives a nightly file of all ecommerce transactions from the previous day. Several segments and activations depend upon calculated insights from the updated data in order to maintain accuracy in the customer's scheduled campaign messages. What should the consultant do to ensure the ecommerce data is ready for use for each of the scheduled activations?
optionA: Use Flow to trigger a change data event on the ecommerce data to refresh calculated insights and segments before the activations are scheduled to run
optionB: Set a refresh schedule for the calculated insights to occur every hour
optionC: Ensure the activations are set to Incremental Activation and automatically publish every hour
optionD: Ensure the segments are set to Rapid Publish and set to refresh every hour
explanation:
Because data arrives nightly and activations depend on calculated insights from that fresh data, the correct approach is to chain the processes: after ingestion completes, use a Flow (triggered by a data action or change event on the data stream) to refresh calculated insights and then refresh segments before activations run. Hourly calculated insight refreshes (B) are not aligned to the nightly ingestion window. Incremental activation (C) and Rapid Publish (D) affect how activations are sent, not the sequencing of dependency refreshes.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_insights.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Which solution provides an easy way to ingest Marketing Cloud subscriber profile attributes into Data Cloud on a daily basis?
optionA: Automation Studio and Profile file API
optionB: Marketing Cloud Connect API
optionC: Marketing Cloud Data Extension Data Stream
optionD: Email Studio Starter Data Bundle
explanation:
The Marketing Cloud Data Extension Data Stream connector allows Data Cloud to directly ingest data from Marketing Cloud Data Extensions on a scheduled basis — including subscriber profile attributes — without requiring custom automation. Automation Studio with Profile file API (A) requires custom scripting and file drops. Marketing Cloud Connect API (B) is primarily for CRM synchronization, not Data Cloud ingestion. The Email Studio Starter Data Bundle (D) is a pre-packaged bundle for email engagement data, not general subscriber profile attributes.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_create_marketing_cloud_data_extension.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: How should a Data Cloud consultant successfully apply consent during segmentation?
optionA: Include the Consent Status from the golden record during activation for any applicable channels of engagement
optionB: Include Party Identification for any applicable channels of engagement in the filter criteria for each segment
optionC: Include the Unified Profile during segmentation for any applicable channels of engagement
optionD: Include the Consent Status for any applicable channels of engagement in the filter criteria for each segment
explanation:
To honor consent during segmentation, the consultant must add the Consent Status field for each relevant engagement channel as a filter criterion in the segment itself. This ensures that only individuals who have given consent for a specific channel (e.g., email, SMS) are included in the segment before activation. Applying consent only at activation (A) is a later control but best practice is to enforce it at segmentation. Party Identification (B) is an identity object, not a consent mechanism. The Unified Profile (C) is the entity being segmented, not a consent filter.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_consent_management.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Northern Trail Outfitters uses B2C Commerce and is exploring implementing Data Cloud to get a unified view of its customers and all their order transactions. What should the consultant keep in mind with regard to historical data ingesting order data using the B2C Commerce Order Bundle?
optionA: The B2C Commerce Order Bundle ingests 12 months of historical data
optionB: The B2C Commerce Order Bundle ingests 6 months of historical data
optionC: The B2C Commerce Order Bundle does not ingest any historical data and only ingests new orders from that point on
optionD: The B2C Commerce Order Bundle ingests 30 days of historical data
explanation:
The B2C Commerce Order Bundle ingests 30 days of historical order data at initial setup. If NTO requires more than 30 days of order history in Data Cloud, a custom extract or additional ingestion method will need to supplement the bundle. This is a key limitation to communicate during scoping.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_create_commerce_cloud_starter_bundle.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Northern Trail Outfitters (NTO) wants to connect their B2C Commerce data with Data Cloud and bring two years of transactional history into Data Cloud. What should NTO use to achieve this?
optionA: B2C Commerce Starter Bundles
optionB: Direct Sales Order entity ingestion
optionC: Direct Sales Product entity ingestion
optionD: B2C Commerce Starter Bundles plus a custom extract
explanation:
The B2C Commerce Starter Bundles only ingest 30 days of historical order data. To bring two years of transactional history, NTO must use the Starter Bundle in combination with a custom extract (e.g., via S3 or Ingestion API) to backfill the remaining historical data. The bundle alone (A) is insufficient. Direct Sales Order or Product entity ingestion (B, C) are not standard Data Cloud ingestion paths for B2C Commerce.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_create_commerce_cloud_starter_bundle.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: A consultant is reviewing a recent activation using engagement-based related attributes but is not seeing any related attributes in their payload for the majority of their segment members. Which two areas should the consultant review to help troubleshoot this issue? (Choose 2)
optionA: The related engagement events occurred within the last 90 days
optionB: The activations are referencing segments that segment on profile data rather than engagement data
optionC: The correct path is selected for the related attributes
optionD: The activated profiles have a Unified Contact Point
explanation:
Two things commonly empty the related-attribute payload. First, the lookback window: Salesforce documents that for engagement data, activation supports a 90-day lookback window, and engagement records outside it aren't considered when selecting output values (A). Note that a profile can still qualify for the segment on an engagement date up to 24 months old, which is exactly why members appear in the activation while their related attributes come back blank. Second, the relationship path: related attributes are reached through a defined path from the activation DMO, so selecting the wrong path returns nothing (C). Segmenting on profile rather than engagement data (B) changes who is in the segment, not whether related attributes populate, and a Unified Contact Point (D) governs contact-point selection rather than related-attribute resolution. Two limits are worth holding onto alongside this: with a rapid segment publish the lookback window shrinks to seven days, and activation supports up to 25 values per related attribute and 300 related attributes per activation.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_considerations_for_related_attributes.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Cumulus Financial needs to create a composite key on an incoming data source that combines the fields Customer Region and Customer Identifier. Which formula function should a consultant use to create a composite key when a primary key is not available in a data stream?
optionA: CONCAT
optionB: COMBIN
optionC: COALE
optionD: CAST
explanation:
CONCAT is the formula function used in Data Cloud data stream formula fields to combine two or more string values into a single value, making it the correct choice for creating a composite key from Customer Region and Customer Identifier. COMBIN is not a Data Cloud formula function. COALE (COALESCE) returns the first non-null value from a list. CAST converts a field from one data type to another.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=xcloud.sdp_recipe_stringfunctions.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_primary_key.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: A customer is concerned that the consolidation rate displayed in the identity resolution is quite low compared to their initial estimations. Which configuration change should a consultant consider in order to increase the consolidation rate?
optionA: Change reconciliation rules to Most Occurring
optionB: Increase the number of matching rules
optionC: Include additional attributes in the existing matching rules
optionD: Reduce the number of matching rules
explanation:
The consolidation rate measures how far source records collapse into unified profiles, so raising it means matching more aggressively. Match rules within a ruleset are evaluated independently — a record pair unified by any one of them is merged — so adding rules gives records more chances to match and drives the rate up (B). The other options all tighten matching or miss the mechanism: adding attributes to an existing rule (C) piles on criteria that must all be satisfied at once, reducing matches; removing rules (D) removes opportunities to match and lowers the rate further; and reconciliation rules (A) only decide which value wins on an already-unified profile, never whether two records match.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_match_rules.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_match_rules_criteria_fuzzy_normalized.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_resolution_troubleshooting_ci_consolidation_rate.htm&language=en_US&type=5

corrected.note: Q24 D->B. More match rules means more chances to match, which raises the consolidation rate; the old answer had the logic inverted.

question: A consultant at Northern Trail Outfitters is implementing Data Cloud and creating an activation target for their segment. For activation membership, which object should the consultant choose?
optionA: Data Model Object
optionB: Data Activation Object
optionC: Data Segmentation Object
optionD: Data Lake Object
explanation:
Activation for Data Cloud Segments defines activation membership as the grouping of fields from different data model objects (DMOs) to include in an activation, and adds that if you use an identity resolution ruleset to unify your data you must use the Unified Individual DMO as the activation membership. So the object chosen for activation membership is a Data Model Object (A). There is no Data Segmentation Object in Data Cloud; the object that records who belongs to a segment is the Segment Membership DMO (type Segment_Membership, for example Individual_SM__dlm), which is itself a DMO rather than a separate class of object. A Data Lake Object (D) holds ingested source data before harmonisation and is not what an activation publishes.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_activation_for_a_segment.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_segment_membership_data.htm&language=en_US&type=5

corrected.note: Answer moved C->A. Data Segmentation Object is an invented entity — Data Cloud has no such object. Activation membership is documented as a grouping of Data Model Objects, and the Unified Individual DMO is required when an identity resolution ruleset is in use.

question: A consultant is troubleshooting a segment error. Which error message is solved by using calculated insights instead of nested segments?
optionA: Segment is too complex
optionB: Multiple population counts are in progress
optionC: Segment population count failed
optionD: Segment can't be published
explanation:
The 'Segment is too complex' error occurs when a segment's query exceeds computational limits — typically due to deep nesting of segments or too many joined DMOs. The recommended resolution is to pre-compute complex logic using Calculated Insights and then reference the insight results as direct attributes in the segment, reducing runtime query complexity. The other errors relate to concurrency (B), infrastructure failures (C), or publish configuration issues (D), not query complexity.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_segmentation_troubleshooting.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: A healthcare client wants to make use of identity resolution, but does not want to risk unifying profiles that may share certain personally identifying information (PII). Which matching rule criteria should a consultant recommend for the most accurate matching results?
optionA: Party Identification on Patient ID
optionB: Exact Last Name and Email
optionC: Email Address and Phone
optionD: Fuzzy First Name, Exact Last Name, and Email
explanation:
In a healthcare context where false positives (incorrectly merging distinct patients) carry serious risk, matching on a unique system-assigned identifier — the Patient ID via the Party Identification object — provides the most precise and deterministic match. Common PII like name and email (B, D) can be shared across family members or patients with similar demographics, risking incorrect unification. Email and phone (C) also carry false-positive risk in healthcare settings.
References:

question: An automotive dealership wants to implement Data Cloud. What is a use case for Data Cloud's capabilities?
optionA: Implement a full archive solution with version management
optionB: Use browser cookies to track visitor activity on the website and display personalized recommendations
optionC: Build a source of truth for consent management across all unified individuals
optionD: Ingest customer interaction across different touch points, harmonize, and build a data model for analytical reporting
explanation:
Data Cloud's core value proposition is ingesting data from multiple sources (dealership CRM, website, service records, marketing), harmonizing it into unified customer profiles, and enabling analytical and activation use cases. This is a textbook Data Cloud use case. Archive with version management (A) is a data governance/DMS capability. Cookie-based personalization (B) is a web analytics / CDP edge use case beyond standard Data Cloud. Consent management as a source of truth (C) is a partial capability, not a primary use case.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_data_cloud.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: A customer needs to integrate in real time with Salesforce CRM. Which feature accomplishes this requirement?
optionA: Streaming transforms
optionB: Data model triggers
optionC: Sales and Service bundle
optionD: Data actions and Lightning web components
explanation:
Streaming transforms in Data Cloud allow real-time processing of data as it arrives from the Salesforce CRM Connector, enabling near-real-time integration. The CRM Connector with streaming capability pushes standard field changes in real time. Data model triggers (B) do not exist as a standard Data Cloud feature. The Sales and Service bundle (C) is a pre-packaged ingestion connector, not a real-time integration mechanism. Data actions with LWCs (D) are used to surface Data Cloud data inside Salesforce UI, not for real-time CRM integration.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_streaming_transform_overview.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_salesforce_crm_connector.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: What should a user do to pause a segment activation with the intent of using that segment again?
optionA: Deactivate the segment
optionB: Delete the segment
optionC: Skip the activation
optionD: Stop the publish schedule
explanation:
To temporarily pause a segment activation while preserving the segment configuration for future use, the correct action is to stop the publish schedule. This halts the activation runs without removing the segment or its activation configuration, making it easy to resume later. Deactivating the segment (A) removes it from active status and may affect downstream dependencies. Deleting (B) is permanent. 'Skip the activation' (C) is not a standard Data Cloud function.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_publish_segment.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Which tool allows users to visualize and analyze unified customer data in Data Cloud?
optionA: Salesforce CLI
optionB: Heroku
optionC: Tableau
optionD: Einstein Analytics
explanation:
Tableau is the recommended and natively integrated tool for visualizing and analyzing unified customer data from Data Cloud. Tableau can connect directly to Data Cloud via the Query API or direct connector to build dashboards and reports on unified profiles. Salesforce CLI (A) is a developer tool for deployment and metadata. Heroku (B) is an application platform. Einstein Analytics / CRM Analytics (D) can connect to Data Cloud but Tableau is the primary visualization tool called out in the Data Cloud ecosystem.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_data_cloud.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Cloud Kicks wants to be able to build a segment of customers who have visited its website within the previous 7 days. Which filter operator on the Engagement Date field fits this use case?
optionA: Is Between
optionB: Greater than Last Number of
optionC: Next Number of Days
optionD: Last Number of Days
explanation:
Last Number Of Days is the rolling relative-date operator: Salesforce defines it as finding audience members where an event occurs in the last number of days until the current day and time, which is exactly "visited within the previous 7 days" (D). Is Between (A) needs two static dates, and Next Number Of Days (C) looks forward. Greater Than Last Number Of Days is a real operator, but it does the opposite of what this use case needs — it finds events occurring *before* the specified number of days, up to the beginning of the current day — so option B is wrong on behaviour rather than on existence. Note the operator list is case-sensitive in the documentation as Last Number Of Days, and date operators evaluate against your Salesforce org time zone.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_datatype_expression_operators.htm&language=en_US&type=5

corrected.note: Answer stands. The old explanation claimed "Greater than Last Number of" is not a standard Data Cloud operator — Greater Than Last Number Of Days is documented, and it selects events older than the window rather than not existing.

question: The recruiting team at Cumulus Financial wants to identify which candidates have browsed the jobs page on its website at least twice within the last 24 hours. They want the information about these candidates to be available for segmentation in Data Cloud and the candidates added to their recruiting system. Which feature should a consultant recommend to achieve this goal?
optionA: Streaming data transform
optionB: Streaming insight
optionC: Calculated insight
optionD: Batch data transform
explanation:
The stem imposes two requirements, and one of them is decisive: the result must be available for segmentation. Streaming insights cannot be used in the segmentation or activation phases of Data Cloud, which rules out option B however well its real-time character otherwise fits a 24-hour window. A calculated insight can aggregate the visit count per candidate and is usable as a segmentation attribute (C), and the resulting segment can then be activated to the recruiting system, satisfying both halves of the requirement. Streaming and batch data transforms (A and D) reshape data without evaluating a threshold condition at all.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_insights.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_calculated_insights_in_segments.htm&language=en_US&type=5

corrected.note: Q33 B->C. Streaming insights cannot be used in segmentation, which the stem explicitly requires.

question: How can a consultant modify attribute names to match a naming convention in Cloud File Storage targets?
optionA: Use a formula field to update the field name in an activation
optionB: Update attribute names in the data stream configuration
optionC: Set preferred attribute names when configuring activation
optionD: Update field names in the data model object
explanation:
Activation attribute names are set on the activation itself, not upstream (C). Salesforce documents this as the Output Name field — the preferred name — which by default shows the attribute's API name with system prefixes and suffixes stripped, and which you override to match the destination's naming convention. Data 360 then uses that value as the column header in the activated file. Output names must be unique across every attribute in the activation, including attributes drawn from different DMOs, and may contain only alphanumeric characters. Renaming in the data stream (B) or on the data model object (D) would change the source for every downstream consumer, and a formula field (A) derives a value rather than renaming a column.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_preferred_attribute_name.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Cumulus Financial uses Service Cloud as its CRM and stores mobile phone, home phone, and work phone as three separate fields for its customers on the Contact record. The company plans to use Data Cloud and ingest the Contact object via the CRM Connector. What is the most efficient approach that a consultant should take when ingesting this data to ensure all the different phone numbers are properly mapped and available for use in activation?
optionA: Ingest the Contact object and map the Work Phone, Mobile Phone, and Home Phone to the Contact Point Phone data map object from the Contact data stream
optionB: Ingest the Contact object and use streaming transforms to normalize the phone numbers from the Contact data stream into a separate Phone data lake object (DLO) that contains three rows, and then map this new DLO to the Contact Point Phone data map object
optionC: Ingest the Contact object and then create a calculated insight to normalize the phone numbers, and then map to the Contact Point Phone data map object
optionD: Ingest the Contact object and create formula fields in the Contact data stream on the phone numbers, and then map to the Contact Point Phone data map object
explanation:
The Contact Point Phone DMO expects one row per phone number. Since the Contact record has three phone fields (columns), they must be pivoted into rows before mapping. The correct approach is to use a streaming transform to normalize the three phone column values into a new DLO with three rows per contact — one per phone type — which can then be mapped to the Contact Point Phone DMO. Direct mapping of three columns to Contact Point Phone (A) would only capture one phone per record. Calculated insights (C) are not designed for data normalization into new DLOs. Formula fields (D) transform values within a row but don't pivot columns into rows.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_streaming_transform_overview.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_contact_points.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: A user is not seeing suggested values from newly-modeled data when building a segment. What is causing this issue?
optionA: Value suggestion will only return results for the first 50 values of a specific attribute
optionB: Value suggestion can only work on direct attributes and not related attributes
optionC: Value suggestion requires Data Aware Specialist permissions at a minimum
optionD: Value suggestion is still processing and takes up to 24 hours to be available
explanation:
Value suggestions are computed asynchronously after data is modeled, and Salesforce states plainly that it can take up to 24 hours for suggested values to appear — which is why a user who has just modeled new data sees nothing (D). Three details are worth holding onto from the same page: value suggestions can be enabled for up to 500 attributes across the org, suggested values are retained for 30 days, and for an attribute with more than 1,000 values the 1,000 most frequently occurring values are shown alphabetically. Option A's "first 50 values" is not a Data Cloud limit. Option B is not the cause here either, though it is not simply false: when the DMO's category is Other, value suggestion is available for one-to-one and many-to-one relationships and is not available for one-to-many. Permissions (C) govern access rather than suggestion availability.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_suggested_values_in_segments.htm&language=en_US&type=5

corrected.note: Answer stands. The old explanation asserted that the 50-value limit in option A "is real" — it is not. The documented cap is the 1,000 most frequently occurring values, and the relationship-type caveat in option B was dismissed as simply false when it holds for Other-category DMOs on one-to-many relationships.

question: A consultant wants to make sure address details from customer orders are selected as best to save to the unified profile. What should the consultant do to achieve this?
optionA: Select the address details on the Contact Point Address. Change the reconciliation rules for the specific address attributes to Source Priority and move the Individual DMO to the bottom
optionB: Use the default reconciliation rules for Contact Point Address
optionC: Select the address details on the Contact Point Address. Change the reconciliation rules for the specific address attributes to Source Priority and move the Order DMO to the top
optionD: Change the default reconciliation rules for Individual to Source Priority
explanation:
The intent of option C — prefer the order source over other sources — is the right instinct, and it is kept as the answer because it is what this item tests. Be aware of two things the current documentation says, though. Reconciliation rules do not apply to contact points such as email, phone or address: all contact points remain part of the unified profile, and Salesforce directs you to the source priority order on the activation to deliver a contact point from the desired source to a target. And the Source Priority reconciliation rule sorts data lake objects, not data model objects, from most to least preferred. So on a current org the reliable way to make order-sourced addresses reach a destination is source priority on the activation, which is the mechanism this deck keys correctly elsewhere.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_reconciliation_rules.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_contact_points.htm&language=en_US&type=5

corrected.note: Item defect: the keyed action is configuring reconciliation rules on Contact Point Address, but Salesforce documents that reconciliation rules do not apply to contact points, and that Source Priority sorts DLOs rather than DMOs. Key kept as the closest to the item's intent; no option describes the documented mechanism.

question: A new user of Data Cloud only needs to be able to review individual rows of ingested data and validate that it has been modeled successfully to its linked data model object. The user will also need to make changes if required. What is the minimum permission set needed to accommodate this use case?
optionA: Data Cloud for Marketing Specialist
optionB: Data Cloud Admin
optionC: Data Cloud User
optionD: Data Cloud for Marketing Data Aware Specialist
explanation:
The permission set that lets a user inspect ingested rows and still change the modeling is the Data Aware Specialist (D) — Salesforce describes it as being able to map data to the data model and create data streams, identity resolution rulesets, and calculated insights, which covers both halves of the requirement. Data Cloud User (C) is view-only and so cannot make changes, and the Architect set (option B's Data Cloud Admin) grants all functionality including Data Cloud Setup, which is more than the minimum asked for. Note that the option text uses pre-September-2025 naming: as of 4 Sept 2025 the standard permission sets were renamed, and this one is now simply Data Cloud Data Aware Specialist, while Data Cloud Admin is now Data Cloud Architect.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_userpermissions.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Cumulus Financial wants to be able to track the daily transaction volume of each of its customers in real time and send out a notification as soon as it detects volume outside a customer's normal range. What should a consultant do to accommodate this request?
optionA: Use a calculated insight paired with a flow
optionB: Use streaming data transform with a flow
optionC: Use a streaming insight paired with a data action
optionD: Use streaming data transform combined with a data action
explanation:
This use case requires real-time monitoring and immediate notification — classic streaming insight + data action pattern. A streaming insight evaluates transaction volume against a threshold (normal range) as transactions arrive in near-real time. When the threshold condition is met, the associated data action fires the notification. Calculated insights (A) are batch-processed and too slow for real-time detection. Streaming data transforms (B, D) reshape incoming data but don't evaluate threshold conditions or trigger notifications.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_insights.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: A Data Cloud consultant is evaluating the initial phase of the Data Cloud lifecycle for a company. Which action is essential to effectively begin the Data Cloud lifecycle?
optionA: Identify use cases and the required data sources and data quality
optionB: Analyze and partition the data into data spaces
optionC: Migrate the existing data into the Customer 360 Data Model
optionD: Use calculated insights to determine the benefits of Data Cloud for this company
explanation:
The Data Cloud lifecycle begins with discovery and scoping — identifying the business use cases, which data sources are needed to support them, and assessing data quality. Without this foundational step, all subsequent configuration decisions lack business alignment. Data space partitioning (B), data migration (C), and calculated insights (D) are all later phases that depend on the use-case and data-source inventory established in the first phase.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_data_cloud.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: A Data Cloud consultant tries to save a new 1-to-1 relationship between the Account DMO and Contact Point Address DMO but gets an error. What should the consultant do to fix this error?
optionA: Change the cardinality to many-to-one to accommodate multiple contacts per account
optionB: Map Account to Contact Point Email and Contact Point Phone also
optionC: Map additional fields to the Contact Point Address DMO
optionD: Make sure that the total account records are high enough for identity resolution
explanation:
Contact Point Address is a standard DMO with required fields. A 1-to-1 relationship save error typically occurs because mandatory fields on the Contact Point Address DMO have not been mapped. Mapping additional required fields resolves the validation error. Changing cardinality (A) would be appropriate if the business requirement changed, not to fix a save error. Mapping other contact point objects (B) is unrelated. Record volume (D) has no bearing on relationship configuration errors.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_required_data_mappings.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_map_custom_data_model_objects.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Which consideration related to the way Data Cloud ingests CRM data is true?
optionA: CRM data cannot be manually refreshed and must wait for the next scheduled synchronization
optionB: The CRM Connector's synchronization times can be customized to up to 15-minute intervals
optionC: Formula fields are refreshed at regular sync intervals and are updated at the next full refresh
optionD: The CRM Connector allows standard fields to stream into Data Cloud in real time
explanation:
The Salesforce CRM Connector supports real-time streaming of standard field changes — when a standard field on a CRM object is updated, that change is streamed into Data Cloud near-instantaneously. CRM data can be manually refreshed (A is false). Synchronization intervals are not customizable to 15 minutes (B is false — the connector runs on a fixed schedule). Formula fields are only updated on a full refresh cycle, not incremental sync (C is partially true but D is the correct true statement from the options).
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_salesforce_crm_connector.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_data_stream_schedule.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: A customer has a requirement to be able to view the last time each segment was published within their Data Cloud org. Which two features should the consultant recommend to best address this requirement? (Choose 2)
optionA: Profile Explorer
optionB: Calculated insight
optionC: Dashboard
optionD: Report
explanation:
Segment publish history data is surfaced through standard Salesforce reporting objects. Dashboards (C) and Reports (D) built on the Segment object or related Data Cloud reporting objects can display the last publish time for each segment. Profile Explorer (A) is used to inspect individual unified profiles, not segment-level metadata. Calculated Insights (B) are for computing metrics from data model objects, not for reporting on segment publish times.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_publish_segment.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Which permission setting should a consultant check if the custom Salesforce CRM object is not available in New Data Stream configuration?
optionA: Confirm the Create object permission is enabled in the Data Cloud org
optionB: Confirm the View All object permission is enabled in the source Salesforce CRM org
optionC: Confirm the Ingest Object permission is enabled in the Salesforce CRM org
optionD: Confirm that the Modify Object permission is enabled in the Data Cloud org
explanation:
When a custom object does not appear in the New Data Stream configuration for the CRM Connector, the most common cause is that the connected user in the source Salesforce CRM org does not have View All permission on that custom object. The CRM Connector uses the source org's API to list available objects — if the connected user can't see the object, it won't appear. Permissions in the Data Cloud org (A, D) control Data Cloud-side access, not CRM object visibility. 'Ingest Object' (C) is not a standard Salesforce permission.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_create_crm_data_stream.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_salesforce_crm_connector.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Northern Trail Outfitters uploads new customer data to an Amazon S3 Bucket on a daily basis to be ingested in Data Cloud. Based on this, a calculated insight is created that shows the total spend per customer in the last 30 days. In which sequence should each process be run to ensure that freshly imported data is ready and available to use for any segment?
optionA: Refresh Data Stream > Identity Resolution > Calculated Insight
optionB: Refresh Data Stream > Calculated Insight > Identity Resolution
optionC: Calculated Insight > Refresh Data Stream > Identity Resolution
optionD: Identity Resolution > Refresh Data Stream > Calculated Insight
explanation:
The correct sequence in the Data Cloud pipeline is: (1) Refresh Data Stream — ingest the new S3 data into the data lake; (2) Run Identity Resolution — merge the new raw data into unified profiles; (3) Refresh Calculated Insight — compute the 30-day spend metric against the freshly unified profile data. Calculating insights before identity resolution (B) means the metric runs on unresolved data. Running identity resolution before ingestion (D) processes stale data. Computing insights first (C) makes no sense without the data in place.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_identity_resolution.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_insights.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: A user has built a segment in Data Cloud and is in the process of creating an activation. When selecting related attributes, they cannot find a specific set of attributes they know to be related to the individual. Which statement explains why these attributes are not available?
optionA: The segment is not segmenting on profile data
optionB: The attributes are being used in another activation
optionC: The desired attributes reside on different related paths
optionD: Activations can only include 1-to-1 attributes
explanation:
In Data Cloud activations, related attributes must be reachable via the same DMO relationship path. If the desired attributes exist on a different path from the one already selected in the activation, they will not appear in the attribute picker. Each activation can only traverse one related path at a time (prior to multi-path support). Segmenting on profile vs. other data (A) affects the segment, not activation attribute availability. Attributes being used elsewhere (B) does not block them. Activations support 1-to-many related attributes, not just 1-to-1 (D is false).
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_considerations_for_related_attributes.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: To import campaign members into a campaign in Salesforce CRM, a user wants to export the segment to Amazon S3. The resulting file needs to include the Salesforce CRM Campaign ID in the name. What are two ways to achieve this outcome? (Choose 2)
optionA: Include campaign identifier in the activation name
optionB: Hard code the campaign identifier as a new attribute in the campaign activation
optionC: Include campaign identifier in the filename specification
optionD: Include campaign identifier in the segment name
explanation:
Data Cloud's Amazon S3 activation generates filenames based on the activation name and the filename specification configured in the activation settings. Including the Campaign ID in the activation name (A) embeds it in the default filename. Including it in the filename specification (C) gives explicit control over the output file name. Hard coding it as an attribute (B) would add it as a data column, not in the filename. Including it in the segment name (D) doesn't influence the activation output filename.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_file_name_examples.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_find_segments_in_cloud_file_storage.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: During an implementation project, a consultant completed ingestion of all data streams for their customer. Prior to segmenting and acting on that data, which additional configuration is required?
optionA: Data Activation
optionB: Calculated Insights
optionC: Data Mapping
optionD: Identity Resolution
explanation:
After data streams are ingested and mapped, Identity Resolution must be run before segmentation can operate on unified profiles. Identity Resolution merges records from multiple sources into Unified Individuals — the entity that segmentation targets. Without it, segments would run on unresolved raw data rather than the consolidated 360-degree view. Data Mapping (C) is part of the ingestion step, not a post-ingestion requirement. Calculated Insights (B) and Activation (A) come after segmentation, not before.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_identity_resolution.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: A user needs permissions to access Data Cloud to create, manage, and activate segments. However, the user should not be allowed to create reports or manage data sources. Which permission set should the consultant assign?
optionA: Data Cloud Marketing Specialist
optionB: Data Cloud Marketing Manager
optionC: Data Cloud Data Aware Specialist
optionD: Data Cloud User
explanation:
The set scoped to segmentation work without data-source or reporting rights is the one this option calls Data Cloud Marketing Specialist (A). Salesforce describes it as being able to create segments, with full access to Segment, Activations, Query Editor, Data Actions and Data Transforms, and view-only access to Data Streams, DLOs, DMOs, Identity Resolution, Insights and Profile Explorer — so the user can build and activate segments but cannot manage data sources. The Marketing Manager set (B) adds overall segmentation strategy and the creation of activation targets, Data Aware Specialist (C) carries the data-modeling rights this user is meant not to have, and Data Cloud User (D) is view-only. Note the naming: as of 4 Sept 2025 this permission set is called Data Cloud Activation Specialist, and Data Cloud Marketing Manager is now Data Cloud Activation Manager.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_userpermissions.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: A customer creates a large segment of customers that placed orders in the last 30 days, and adds related attributes from orders to the activation. Upon checking the activation in Marketing Cloud, they notice it contains orders that are older than 30 days. What should a consultant do to resolve this issue?
optionA: Use data graphs that contain only 30 days of data
optionB: Apply a data space filter to exclude orders older than 30 days
optionC: Apply a filter to Purchase Order Date to exclude orders older than 30 days
optionD: Use SQL in Marketing Cloud Engagement to remove orders older than 30 days
explanation:
When related attributes are added to an activation, the segment filter (last 30 days) controls which individuals are included, but all related records for those individuals are returned unless a related attribute filter is applied. To restrict the activation to only include orders from the last 30 days, a filter on the Purchase Order Date must be added within the related attribute configuration in the activation itself. Data space filters (B) operate at the data visibility level, not activation attribute filtering. SQL in Marketing Cloud (D) is a post-activation workaround. Data graphs (A) are not relevant to this scenario.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_considerations_for_related_attributes.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: A consultant wants to confirm the Identity resolution they just set up. Which two features can the consultant use to validate the data on a unified profile? (Choose 2)
optionA: Identity Resolution
optionB: Data Actions
optionC: Data Explorer
optionD: Query API
explanation:
Data Explorer lets you inspect the rows of any DLO or DMO, including the Unified Individual, to confirm that source records merged as expected (C), and the Query API returns unified profile data programmatically so field values and linkages can be verified outside the UI (D). Data Actions (B) publish events downstream and are not an inspection surface. Option A is the weak part of this item rather than a clean distractor: Identity Resolution does carry a validation surface of its own — the Resolution Summary reports match and reconciliation statistics after each ruleset run, and this deck keys exactly that as a valid way to validate a unified profile elsewhere. Treat C and D as the answer because they inspect the resulting data directly, but do not take from this item that identity resolution offers nothing to check.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_data_explorer.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_resolution_summary.htm&language=en_US&type=5

corrected.note: Item defect: three of the four options are defensible. The Resolution Summary is a documented way to validate identity resolution output, so option A is not simply wrong, and this deck's own question on the same topic keys Identity Resolution as a validation feature. Key kept as the two that inspect profile data directly.

question:
When creating a segment on an individual, what is the result of using two separate containers linked by an AND as shown below?
GoodsProduct | Count | At Least | 1 / Color | Is Equal To | red
AND
GoodsProduct | Count | At Least | 1 / PrimaryProductCategory | Is Equal To | shoes
optionA: Individuals who purchased at least one of any red product and also purchased at least one pair of shoes
optionB: Individuals who purchased at least one red shoes as a single line item in a purchase
optionC: Individuals who made a purchase of at least one red shoes and nothing else
optionD: Individuals who purchased at least one of any red product or purchased at least one pair of shoes
explanation:
Attributes placed in the same container act on the same data row of the container's object; attributes placed in separate containers are evaluated independently of each other. Salesforce's own worked example is this question: put yellow in one container and scarf in another, and the query engine looks for customers who purchased any yellow product and purchased a scarf of any color — not a yellow scarf. So two containers joined by AND return individuals who bought at least one red product and, separately, at least one pair of shoes (A). Option B is what you would get by putting Color and PrimaryProductCategory in the same container, C adds an exclusivity the filter never expresses, and D is OR logic.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.c360_a_container_basics.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: A consultant is helping a beauty company ingest its profile data into Data Cloud. The company's source data includes several fields, such as eye color, skin type, and hair color, that are not fields in the standard Individual data model object (DMO). What should the consultant recommend to map this data to be used for both segmentation and identity resolution?
optionA: Create a custom DMO from scratch that has all fields that are needed
optionB: Create a custom DMO with only the additional fields and map it to the standard Individual DMO
optionC: Create custom fields on the standard Individual DMO
optionD: Duplicate the standard Individual DMO and add the additional fields
explanation:
The correct approach is to add custom fields directly to the standard Individual DMO. This keeps all individual profile data — standard and custom — on the same object, making it available for both segmentation (which operates on the Individual/Unified Individual) and identity resolution (which uses the Individual DMO). Creating a separate custom DMO (A, B) would require additional relationship mapping and won't be used directly in identity resolution. Duplicating the standard DMO (D) is not a supported pattern.
References:

https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_required_data_mappings.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Northern Trail Outfitters wants to implement Data Cloud and has several use cases in mind. Which two use cases are considered a good fit for Data Cloud? (Choose 2)
optionA: To ingest and unify data from various sources to reconcile customer identity
optionB: To create and orchestrate cross-channel marketing messages
optionC: To use harmonized data to more accurately understand the customer and business impact
optionD: To eliminate the need for separate business intelligence and IT data management tools
explanation:
Data Cloud's core capabilities are (A) ingesting data from multiple sources and unifying it through identity resolution to create a single customer view, and (C) using that harmonized unified data to generate insights about customers and business impact. Cross-channel message orchestration (B) is the domain of Marketing Cloud Journeys, not Data Cloud itself. Eliminating BI and IT tools (D) is not a Data Cloud value proposition — it complements those tools rather than replacing them.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_data_cloud.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Cumulus Financial offers both business and personal loans. Records in the Contact DLO can be useful for both groups since individual customers may have both business and personal loans. However, for legal reasons, the two groups must be kept separate. How should Cumulus Financial solve this business requirement?
optionA: Duplicate the Individual DMO
optionB: Duplicate the Contact DLO
optionC: Create two identity resolution rules in the same data space
optionD: Use two data spaces
explanation:
Data spaces provide complete logical separation of data within a single Data Cloud org — separate identity resolution, segmentation, and activation contexts. For legal requirements that mandate separation between business and personal loan customers, two data spaces is the correct architectural pattern. The same Contact DLO data can be referenced in both spaces as needed. Duplicating the Individual DMO (A) or Contact DLO (B) creates maintenance overhead without enforcing legal separation. Two identity resolution rulesets in the same data space (C) share the same data pool and do not provide legal separation.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_data_spaces.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Which two common use cases can be addressed with Data Cloud? (Choose 2)
optionA: Understand and act upon customer data to drive more relevant experiences
optionB: Govern enterprise data lifecycle through a centralized set of policies and processes
optionC: Harmonize data from multiple sources with a standardized and extendable data model
optionD: Safeguard critical business data by serving as a centralized system for backup and disaster recovery
explanation:
Data Cloud's primary use cases are: (A) creating unified customer profiles and activating them to deliver personalized, relevant experiences; and (C) harmonizing data from disparate sources into the standardized Customer 360 Data Model. Enterprise data governance lifecycle (B) and backup/disaster recovery (D) are not Data Cloud use cases — these are addressed by dedicated data governance platforms and backup solutions respectively.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_data_cloud.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Northern Trail Outfitters wants to be able to calculate each customer's lifetime value (LTV) but also create breakdowns of the revenue sourced by website, mobile app, and retail channels. What should a consultant use to address this use case in Data Cloud?
optionA: Flow Orchestration
optionB: Nested segments
optionC: Metrics on metrics
optionD: Streaming data transform
explanation:
Metrics on metrics (also known as multi-dimensional calculated insights) allow a consultant to first calculate a base metric (e.g., total revenue per channel) and then compute a higher-level metric on top of it (e.g., LTV as the sum of channel revenues). This is exactly what is needed — LTV overall plus channel-level breakdowns. Flow Orchestration (A) automates processes, not metric computation. Nested segments (B) filter populations, not compute revenue metrics. Streaming transforms (D) reshape incoming data, not compute aggregated insights.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_insights.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: A marketing manager at Northern Trail Outfitters wants to improve marketing return on investment (ROI) by tapping into Insights from Data Cloud Segment Intelligence. Which permission set does a user need to set this up?
optionA: Data Cloud Data Aware Specialist
optionB: Data Cloud User
optionC: Cloud Marketing Manager
optionD: Data Cloud Admin
explanation:
Setting up Segment Intelligence is administrative work — connecting sources and configuring the feature — so it needs the permission set that grants all Data Cloud functionality, which this option calls Data Cloud Admin (D). Data Aware Specialist (A) covers data mapping and modeling, Data Cloud User (B) is view-only, and Cloud Marketing Manager (C) is not a permission set name at all. Note the naming: as of 4 Sept 2025 the standard permission sets were renamed and this one is now Data Cloud Architect, described as giving access to all functionality within Data 360 including Data Cloud Setup, data mapping, data streams, identity resolution rulesets and insights.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_userpermissions.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: A user wants to be able to create a multi-dimensional metric to identify unified individual lifetime value (LTV). Which sequence of data model object (DMO) joins is necessary within the calculated insight to enable this calculation?
optionA: Unified Individual > Unified Link Individual > Sales Order
optionB: Unified Individual > Individual > Sales Order
optionC: Sales Order > Individual > Unified Individual
optionD: Sales Order > Unified Individual
explanation:
To calculate LTV at the Unified Individual level, the calculated insight must join from Unified Individual through Unified Link Individual (the bridge object that maps unified profiles back to their source Individual records) and then to Sales Order (which holds transactional data). This is the correct join path in the Data Cloud unified data model. Joining directly to Individual (B) skips the unified layer. Joining from Sales Order upward (C) is an unconventional path that doesn't reflect the calculated insight join direction. Skipping Unified Link Individual (D) is not a valid join path.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_identity_resolution.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_insights.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: A consultant is planning the ingestion of a data stream that has profile information including a mobile phone number. To ensure that the phone number can be used for future SMS campaigns, they need to confirm the phone number field is in the proper E164 Phone Number format. However, the phone numbers in the file appear to be in varying formats. What is the most efficient way to guarantee that the various phone number formats are standardized?
optionA: Create a formula field to standardize the format
optionB: Edit and update the data in the source system prior to sending to Data Cloud
optionC: Assign the PhoneNumber field type when creating the data stream
optionD: Create a calculated insight after ingestion
explanation:
Assigning the phone data type does not standardize anything. Salesforce states it plainly: Data 360 doesn't validate the format of the phone number, the phone data type is modeled on the text data type, and any valid text value is accepted for ingestion into a phone field. Choosing that type only marks the field's intent. The same page points at the actual mechanism — formula functions that work with text values accept phone data type input, and you can convert the text output of those functions back into a phone data type — so a formula field applied at ingestion is what normalizes the varying formats into E164 (A). Fixing the data upstream (B) works but is the opposite of efficient and is often outside your control, and a calculated insight (D) computes metrics after ingestion rather than reshaping the stored field. The E164 requirement itself is real: it is the only format accepted for SMS sending, so the normalization has to happen somewhere.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_data_types.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_considerations_formula_fields.htm&language=en_US&type=5

corrected.note: Answer moved C->A. The keyed claim that assigning the PhoneNumber field type standardizes numbers into E164 is contradicted by the Data Types page, which says Data 360 does not validate phone format and accepts any text. The same page names formula functions as the supported way to transform the value.

question: What is the result of a segmentation criteria filtering on City | Is Equal To | 'San Jose'?
optionA: Cities containing 'San Jose', 'SAN JOSE', 'san jose', or 'San jose'
optionB: Cities only containing 'San Jose' or 'san jose'
optionC: Cities only containing 'San Jose'
optionD: Cities only containing 'San Jose' or 'SAN JOSE'
explanation:
Salesforce documents segmentation queries as honoring exact matching on special characters and accents while not being case-sensitive. So 'Is Equal To' on City matches every casing of the entered value — 'San Jose', 'SAN JOSE', 'san jose', and 'San jose' alike (A) — and the remaining options each admit only a subset of those casings. Two boundaries are worth holding onto: case-insensitive is not a partial match, so 'San Jose, CA' is still excluded; and accents are matched exactly, which is why Salesforce's own example notes that a query for 'Canon City' finds 'canon city' but does not find 'Cañon City'.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_datatype_expression_operators.htm&language=en_US&type=5
