question: Which information is provided in a .csv file when activating to Amazon S3?
optionA: An audit log showing the user who activated the segment and when it was activated
optionB: The activated data payload
optionC: The metadata regarding the segment definition
optionD: The manifest of origin sources within Data Cloud
explanation:
When Data Cloud activates to Amazon S3, the .csv file contains the activated data payload — the segment members and their selected attributes (contact points, related attributes, etc.). The .json file (not .csv) contains the metadata about the segment definition, activation ID, and schema. Audit logs (A) are available in Salesforce's audit trail, not in the S3 output. The manifest of origin sources (D) is also in the .json manifest file, not the .csv.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_find_segments_in_cloud_file_storage.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: A customer has a Master Customer table from their CRM to ingest into Data Cloud. The table contains a name and primary email address, along with other personally identifiable information (PII). How should the fields be mapped to support identity resolution?
optionA: Create a new custom object with fields that directly match the incoming table
optionB: Map all fields to the Customer object
optionC: Map name to the Individual object and email address to the Contact Point Email object
optionD: Map all fields to the Individual object, adding a custom field for the email address
explanation:
For identity resolution to work correctly, name fields must be mapped to the Individual DMO and email addresses must be mapped to the Contact Point Email DMO. This separation follows the Data Cloud standard data model — the Individual DMO holds identity attributes, while Contact Point objects hold contact details. Identity resolution matching rules reference these specific DMOs. Mapping everything to a custom object (A) or the Individual DMO alone (D) prevents the standard identity resolution rules from functioning. There is no standard 'Customer' object in Data Cloud's data model (B).
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_required_data_mappings.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_contact_points.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Northern Trail Outfitters (NTO) creates a calculated insight to compute recency, frequency, monetary (RFM) scores on its unified individuals. NTO then creates a segment based on these scores that it activates to a Marketing Cloud activation target. Which two actions are required when configuring the activation? (Choose 2)
optionA: Add additional attributes
optionB: Choose a segment
optionC: Select contact points
optionD: Add the calculated insight in the activation
explanation:
When configuring any Marketing Cloud activation in Data Cloud, two required actions are: (B) Choose a segment — the activation must be linked to a segment that defines the population to activate; and (C) Select contact points — Marketing Cloud requires a contact point (e.g., email address) to identify where to send the activation. Additional attributes (A) are optional enhancements. The calculated insight (D) is already embedded in the segment's criteria — it does not need to be separately added to the activation.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_activation_for_a_segment.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_contact_points.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: A Data Cloud consultant recently added a new data source and mapped some of the data to a new custom data model object (DMO) that they want to use for creating segments. However, they cannot view the newly created DMO when trying to create a new segment. What is the cause of this issue?
optionA: Data has not yet been ingested into the DMO
optionB: The new DMO is not of category Profile
optionC: The new DMO does not have a relationship to the individual DMO
optionD: Segmentation is only supported for the Individual and Unified Individual DMOs
explanation:
In Data Cloud, only DMOs of category Profile are available as the primary segmentation object (the 'Segment On' object). If the newly created custom DMO was mapped with the Engagement or Other category, it will not appear in the segment builder as a segmentation target. The DMO must be assigned the Profile category for direct segmentation. Lack of ingested data (A) doesn't hide the DMO from the segment builder. A relationship to Individual (C) enables related-attribute segmentation but is not required for the DMO to appear. Segmentation supports multiple profile-category DMOs, not just Individual (D is false).
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_category.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_segments.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Cumulus Financial created a segment called Multiple Investments that contains individuals who have invested in two or more mutual funds. The company plans to send an email to this segment regarding a new mutual fund offering, and wants to personalize the email content with information about each customer's current mutual fund investments. How should the Data Cloud consultant configure this activation?
optionA: Include Fund Type equal to 'Mutual Fund' as a related attribute. Configure an activation based on the new segment with no additional attributes
optionB: Choose the Multiple Investments segment, choose the Email contact point, add related attribute Fund Name, and add related attribute filter for Fund Type equal to 'Mutual Fund'
optionC: Choose the Multiple Investments segment, choose the Email contact point, and add related attribute Fund Type
optionD: Include Fund Name and Fund Type by default for post processing in the target system
explanation:
The activation must: (1) use the Multiple Investments segment; (2) select the Email contact point for delivery; (3) include Fund Name as a related attribute for personalization content; and (4) add a related attribute filter for Fund Type = 'Mutual Fund' to ensure only mutual fund investments (not other investment types) are included in the payload. Option C omits the filter so non-mutual-fund investments could be included. Option A configures a filter but no segment. Option D defers personalization logic to the target system, which is inefficient.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_considerations_for_related_attributes.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_contact_points.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Which method should a consultant use when performing aggregations in windows of 15 minutes on data collected via the Interaction SDK or Mobile SDK?
optionA: Batch transform
optionB: Calculated insight
optionC: Streaming insight
optionD: Formula fields
explanation:
Streaming insights are designed for near-real-time aggregations over rolling time windows on streaming data — including data arriving via the Interaction SDK (web events) and Mobile SDK. A 15-minute aggregation window is a classic streaming insight use case. Batch transforms (A) and Calculated Insights (B) are scheduled batch operations not suited for sub-hour rolling windows. Formula fields (D) operate at the field level during ingestion, not for aggregations over time windows.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_insights.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: How does Data Cloud ensure high availability and fault tolerance for customer data?
optionA: By distributing data across multiple regions and data centers
optionB: By using a data center with robust backups
optionC: By implementing automatic data recovery procedures
optionD: By limiting data access to essential personnel
explanation:
Data Cloud is built on Salesforce's hyperforce infrastructure, which distributes data across multiple geographic regions and data centers. This distributed architecture provides high availability (no single point of failure) and fault tolerance (data remains accessible even if one region experiences an outage). Single data center with backups (B) is a less resilient pattern. Automatic recovery (C) is a feature but not the primary mechanism for high availability. Access control (D) is a security measure, not a high availability strategy.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_data_cloud.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Which configuration supports separate Amazon S3 buckets for data ingestion and activation?
optionA: Dedicated S3 data sources in Data Cloud setup
optionB: Multiple S3 connectors in Data Cloud setup
optionC: Dedicated S3 data sources in activation setup
optionD: Separate user credentials for data stream and activation target
explanation:
Data Cloud supports configuring separate Amazon S3 connections — one configured as the ingestion data source (in Data Cloud Setup > Connected Apps / Data Streams) and another as the activation target. Using dedicated S3 data sources in Data Cloud setup for ingestion, and a separate S3 bucket configured in the activation target settings, allows complete separation of ingestion and activation buckets. Multiple connectors (B) is the mechanism, but 'dedicated S3 data sources in Data Cloud setup' (A) is the specific correct phrasing. Separate credentials alone (D) don't enforce bucket separation.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_data_ingestion.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_create_cloud_file_storage_activation_target.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: A consultant is ingesting a list of employees from their human resources database that they want to segment on. Which data stream category should the consultant choose when ingesting this data?
optionA: Profile Data
optionB: Contact Data
optionC: Other Data
optionD: Engagement Data
explanation:
Profile is the category for data that describes who someone is, and Salesforce's Category page names this case directly: choose Profile if your dataset is a list of individuals with identifiers, a list of businesses or accounts, or a list of employees or any other population that you want to segment on (A). Employee records from an HR system are exactly that. Engagement (D) is for time-series event data and requires an event date-time field to be nominated at setup, Other (C) is for reference data that is neither, and Contact Data (B) is not a Data Cloud data stream category. Worth remembering when you pick: the category can't be changed after the data stream is saved.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_category.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: A customer has multiple team members who create segment audiences that work in different time zones. One team member works at the home office in the Pacific time zone, that matches the org Time Zone setting. Another team member works remotely in the Eastern time zone. Which user will see their home time zone in the segment and activation schedule areas?
optionA: The team member in the Pacific time zone
optionB: The team member in the Eastern time zone
optionC: Neither team member; Data Cloud shows all schedules in GMT
optionD: Both team members; Data Cloud adjusts the segment and activation schedules to the time zone of the logged-in user
explanation:
Segment and activation schedule fields display the publish schedule start date and time in the logged-in user's time zone, so each team member sees their own local time (D). The org time zone is not irrelevant, though — it still governs other segmentation behaviour, notably the date-based operators such as Last Number Of Days. Two practical consequences: your org sets the publish time zone on the initial segment save, and a later change to the org's time zone is not picked up by existing segments unless you resave them.

https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_time_zones.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_datatype_expression_operators.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: How does identity resolution select attributes for unified individuals when there is conflicting information in the data model?
optionA: Creates additional contact points
optionB: Leverages reconciliation rules
optionC: Creates additional rulesets
optionD: Leverages match rules
explanation:
When multiple source records are merged into a unified individual and those records have conflicting values for the same attribute (e.g., different addresses), identity resolution uses reconciliation rules to determine which value to use on the unified profile. Reconciliation rules can be set to Last Updated, Most Occurring, Source Priority, or other strategies. Match rules (D) are used to determine whether two records represent the same individual — they don't select attribute values. Contact points and rulesets (A, C) are separate constructs.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_reconciliation_rules.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Which statement is true related to batch ingestions from Salesforce CRM?
optionA: When a column is added or removed, the CRM connector performs a full refresh
optionB: The CRM connector performs an incremental refresh when 600K or more deletion records are detected
optionC: The CRM connector's synchronization times can be customized to up to 15-minute intervals
optionD: CRM data cannot be manually refreshed and must wait for the next scheduled synchronization
explanation:
When a schema change occurs on a CRM object — such as adding or removing a field that is part of the data stream — the CRM Connector automatically triggers a full refresh to ensure the data lake is consistent with the new schema. Incremental refreshes handle row-level changes; schema changes require a full reload. The 600K deletion threshold (B) triggers a full refresh for deletions, not an incremental — so B is technically partially correct but A is the cleaner true statement. Synchronization times are not customizable by the user (C is false). CRM data can be manually refreshed (D is false).
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_data_stream_edit_settings.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_crm_store_deleted_data_stream_records.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Which two steps should a consultant take if a successfully configured Amazon S3 data stream fails to refresh with a 'NO FILE FOUND' error message? (Choose 2)
optionA: Check if correct permissions are configured for the Data Cloud user
optionB: Check if the Amazon S3 data source is enabled in Data Cloud Setup
optionC: Check if the file exists in the specified bucket location
optionD: Check if correct permissions are configured for the S3 user
explanation:
A 'NO FILE FOUND' error on an S3 data stream refresh means Data Cloud attempted to read the file and either couldn't find it or couldn't access it. The two areas to investigate are: (A) Permissions for the Data Cloud user/connected credentials — if permissions are misconfigured, Data Cloud cannot read the bucket, which can manifest as a not-found error; and (C) Whether the file actually exists in the configured bucket path — if the upstream process didn't deliver the file, there is nothing to ingest. Checking if the data source is enabled in Setup (B) would prevent configuration at all, not a refresh failure. S3 user permissions (D) overlaps with A but A is the more precise check within Data Cloud's configuration.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_data_streams.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_data_ingestion.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Cumulus Financial is currently using Data Cloud and ingesting transactional data from its backend system via an S3 Connector in upsert mode. During the initial setup six months ago, the company created a formula field in Data Cloud to create a custom classification. It now needs to update this formula to account for more classifications. What should the consultant keep in mind with regard to formula field updates when using the S3 Connector?
optionA: Data Cloud will update the formula for all records at the next incremental upsert refresh
optionB: Data Cloud does not support formula field updates for data streams of type upsert
optionC: Data Cloud will initiate a full refresh of data from S3 and will update the formula on all records
optionD: Data Cloud will only update the formula on a go-forward basis for new records
explanation:
When a formula field is updated on a data stream using the S3 Connector in upsert mode, Data Cloud triggers a full refresh of the data stream — re-ingesting all records from S3 and applying the updated formula to every record. This ensures historical data reflects the new formula logic. An incremental refresh (A) would only process new/changed records, missing historical ones. Formula updates are supported for upsert streams (B is false). Go-forward-only updates (D) would leave historical records with stale formula values.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_full_replace.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_considerations_formula_fields.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: An organization wants to enable users with the ability to identify and select text attributes from a picklist of options. Which Data Cloud feature should help with this use case?
optionA: Value suggestion
optionB: Data harmonization
optionC: Transformation formulas
optionD: Global picklists
explanation:
Value suggestion is the Data Cloud feature that presents users with a dropdown of available attribute values when building segment criteria. When enabled on a DMO attribute, it indexes the distinct values and surfaces them as selectable options in the segment builder, making it easy to pick from known values rather than typing them manually. Data harmonization (B) is a broader concept. Transformation formulas (C) are for field derivation during ingestion. Global picklists (D) are a Salesforce CRM feature, not native to Data Cloud segmentation.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_suggested_values_in_segments.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Northern Trail Outfitters (NTO) wants to send a promotional campaign for customers that have purchased within the past 6 months. The consultant created a segment to meet this requirement. Now, NTO brings an additional requirement to suppress customers who have made purchases within the last week. What should the consultant use to remove the recent customers?
optionA: Batch transforms
optionB: Segmentation exclude rules
optionC: Related attributes
optionD: Streaming insight
explanation:
Segmentation exclude rules (exclusion containers) allow a consultant to add an exclusion condition to an existing segment — in this case, excluding individuals who made a purchase within the last week. This is cleaner than modifying the main segment criteria and clearly communicates the suppression intent. Batch transforms (A) reshape data, not filter segments. Related attributes (C) add data to an activation payload, not exclude segment members. Streaming insights (D) enable real-time event actions, not segment suppression.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_segments.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.c360_a_container_basics.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: During a privacy law discussion with a customer, the customer indicates they need to honor requests for the right to be forgotten. The consultant determines that Consent API will solve this business need. Which two considerations should the consultant inform the customer about? (Choose 2)
optionA: Data deletion requests are reprocessed at 30, 60, and 90 days
optionB: Data deletion requests are processed within 1 hour
optionC: Data deletion requests are submitted for Individual profiles
optionD: Data deletion requests submitted to Data Cloud are passed to all connected Salesforce clouds
explanation:
Two considerations matter when Consent API is used for right-to-be-forgotten. Deletion requests are reprocessed at 30, 60, and 90 days, so that any data for the individual that arrived after the original request is also removed and full deletion can be verified (A), and requests are submitted against Individual profiles, which is the entity Data Cloud deletes by (C). Option D inverts the actual behaviour and is the trap here: a deletion request submitted to Data Cloud is not propagated outward, and Salesforce is explicit that you must submit deletion requests separately in every connected system and Salesforce cloud. The one-hour processing claim (B) is not the documented commitment.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_data_deletion_request.htm&language=en_US&type=5

corrected.note: Q78 C,D->A,C. Deletion requests are reprocessed at 30/60/90 days, and they are NOT propagated to connected clouds — you must submit separately.

question: Which data stream category type should be assigned in order to use the dataset for date and time-based operations in segmentation and calculated insights?
optionA: Individual
optionB: Engagement
optionC: Sales Order
optionD: Profile
explanation:
The Engagement category is required for data streams that will be used in date and time-based operations — such as 'events in the last 7 days' or time-window aggregations in calculated insights and streaming insights. Engagement-type DMOs have an Event Time field that enables temporal filtering and aggregation. Profile-category DMOs (D) are for static identity attributes and do not support the same time-based operations. Individual and Sales Order (A, C) are specific DMO types, not data stream category types.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_category.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: A consultant is building a segment to announce a new product launch for customers that have previously purchased black pants. How should the consultant place attributes for product color and product type from the Order Product object to meet this criteria?
optionA: Place the attribute for product color in one container and the attribute for product type in another container
optionB: Place an attribute for the 'black' calculated insight to dynamically apply
optionC: Place the attributes for product and product type as direct attributes
optionD: Place the attributes for product color and product type in a single container
explanation:
To find customers who purchased black pants — meaning a single product that is both black AND pants — both attributes must be evaluated against the same product record. Placing both Product Color = Black and Product Type = Pants in a single container ensures they are applied as AND conditions on the same Order Product row. Placing them in separate containers (A) evaluates them independently across any product in any order — a customer who bought black shoes and white pants would incorrectly qualify. Direct attributes (C) only work for attributes on the primary segmented DMO, not related objects.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.c360_a_container_basics.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: A segment fails to refresh with the error 'Segment references too many data lake objects (DLOS)'. Which two troubleshooting tips should help remedy this issue? (Choose 2)
optionA: Split the segment into smaller segments
optionB: Use calculated insights in order to reduce the complexity of the segmentation query
optionC: Refine segmentation criteria to limit up to five custom data model objects (DMOs)
optionD: Space out the segment schedules to reduce DLO load
explanation:
When a segment exceeds the DLO reference limit: (A) Splitting the segment into smaller, more focused segments reduces the number of DLOs each individual segment references; and (B) Pre-computing complex multi-DLO logic in a Calculated Insight and referencing that insight in the segment dramatically reduces the number of DLOs the segment query must join at runtime. Limiting to five custom DMOs (C) is a good practice but not a specific documented remedy for this error. Spacing out schedules (D) addresses concurrency, not DLO count.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_segmentation_troubleshooting.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: The Data Cloud admin at Northern Trail Outfitters (NTO) wants to be proactively and immediately informed via Slack and email if any of the data streams fail for any reason. If this happens, a case should also be triggered as part of NTO's existing support and triage process, and reflected in its global monitoring dashboard. What should a consultant recommend for these requirements?
optionA: Data actions
optionB: Data Cloud Query Editor
optionC: Salesforce flows
optionD: Salesforce reports and dashboards
explanation:
Salesforce Flows can monitor Data Cloud data stream failure events and orchestrate multi-step notifications — sending a Slack message, sending an email, creating a Case record, and updating a dashboard — all from a single automation. Flows are the appropriate tool for orchestrating cross-system notifications and record creation based on Data Cloud events. Data actions (A) trigger from insight thresholds, not data stream failures. Query Editor (B) is a manual querying tool. Reports and dashboards (D) display data but don't trigger proactive notifications.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_data_cloud.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: (Variant) A user is not seeing suggested values from newly-modeled data when building a segment. What is causing this issue?
optionA: Value suggestion is still processing and will be available soon
optionB: Value suggestion requires Data Aware Specialist permissions at a minimum
optionC: Value suggestion can only work on direct attributes and not related attributes
optionD: Value suggestion will only return results for the first 50 values of a specific attribute
explanation:
Value suggestions are computed asynchronously after data is modeled, and Salesforce states that it can take up to 24 hours for suggested values to appear — so a user who has just modeled new data is most likely still waiting (A). The other options describe limits that either do not exist or are not the cause here: there is no 50-value cap, the documented behaviour is that an attribute with more than 1,000 values shows the 1,000 most frequently occurring values alphabetically (D); permissions govern access rather than suggestion availability (B); and the relationship caveat in C is narrower than stated — for a DMO in the Other category, value suggestion works on one-to-one and many-to-one relationships and is unavailable on one-to-many. Value suggestions are enabled per Text field from the DMO record home, for up to 500 attributes across the org, and are retained for 30 days.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_suggested_values_in_segments.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: A retail customer wants to bring customer data from different sources and wants to take advantage of identity resolution so that it can be used in segmentation. On which entity should this be segmented for activation membership?
optionA: Subscriber
optionB: Unified Individual
optionC: Unified Contact
optionD: Individual
explanation:
When identity resolution is used, multiple source Individual records are merged into a Unified Individual — the single consolidated customer profile. Segmentation and activation membership should target the Unified Individual to ensure each customer is represented once, with the best available data from all sources. Segmenting on Individual (D) would count each source record separately, potentially activating the same person multiple times. Subscriber (A) and Unified Contact (C) are not standard Data Cloud segmentation entities.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_activation_for_a_segment.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Cumulus Financial is experiencing delays in publishing multiple segments simultaneously. The company wants to avoid reducing the frequency at which segments are published, while retaining the same segments in place today. Which action should a consultant take to alleviate this issue?
optionA: Enable rapid segment publishing to all segments to reduce generation time
optionB: Reduce the number of segments being published
optionC: Increase the Data Cloud segmentation concurrency limit
optionD: Adjust the publish schedule start time of each segment to prevent overlapping processes
explanation:
Raising the limit is a legitimate lever and is kept as the answer: Salesforce says outright that because Data 360 is built to scale, some limits can be adjusted to meet your business needs by working with your account executive, and concurrent publishing is a real constraint — the limits page caps rapid concurrent publishes at 20. Be aware, though, that Salesforce's own remedy for the error "Too many segments are trying to publish at the same time" is to wait for some segments to finish and to change the publish schedule for some of your segments. Staggering publish start times is therefore the documented first response, and it does not conflict with this scenario's constraints — offsetting when each segment starts changes neither the set of segments nor how often each one runs. Reducing the number of segments (B) is the option genuinely ruled out by the requirements, and rapid publish (A) is a per-segment publishing mode rather than a fix for queue contention.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_segmentation_troubleshooting.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_limits_and_guidelines.htm&language=en_US&type=5

corrected.note: Answer stands, but the old explanation dismissed option D on a false premise — it claimed staggering schedules compromises the requirement to keep all segments at the same frequency, which it does not. Salesforce's Troubleshoot Segment Errors page names changing the publish schedule as the remedy for simultaneous publishes, so this item has two defensible options.

question: A consultant is setting up Data Cloud for a multi-brand organization and is using data spaces to segregate its data for various brands. While starting the mapping of a data stream, the consultant notices that they cannot map the object for one of the brands. What should the consultant do to make the object available for a new data space?
optionA: Create a new data stream and map the second data stream to the data space
optionB: Copy data from the default data space to a new DMO using the Data Copy feature and link this DMO to the new data space
optionC: Create a batch transform to split data between different data spaces
optionD: Navigate to the Data Space tab and select the object to be included in the new data space
explanation:
DMOs and DLOs must be explicitly added to a data space before they can be used for mapping within that space. The consultant should navigate to the Data Space configuration and add the relevant object to the target data space. This makes it available for data stream mapping in that space. Creating a new data stream (A) or using Data Copy (B) are unnecessary — the object just needs to be included in the data space. Batch transforms (C) do not control data space membership.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_data_spaces.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: A consultant is working in a customer's Data Cloud org and is asked to delete the existing identity resolution ruleset. Which two impacts should the consultant communicate as a result of this action? (Choose 2)
optionA: All individual data will be removed
optionB: Unified customer data associated with this ruleset will be removed
optionC: Dependencies on data model objects will be removed
optionD: All source profile data will be removed
explanation:
Salesforce states the consequences in one sentence: deleting a ruleset permanently removes all unified customer data, eliminates dependencies on data model objects, stops all processing of the ruleset, and deletes the history of previous runs. That is options B and C. Source profile data is untouched (A and D) — the ingested records remain in the data lake and can be unified again by a new ruleset, which is why the loss is of the unified output rather than the raw data. Two practical points: deletion takes up to 24 hours to complete and previous unification data can't be recovered afterwards, so where the goal is to change matching behaviour while keeping the same ruleset name and ID, update the match or reconciliation rules instead of deleting.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_identity_resolution_deletion.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: A consultant is discussing the benefits of Data Cloud with a customer that has multiple disjointed data sources. Which two functional areas should the consultant highlight in relation to managing customer data? (Choose 2)
optionA: Data Harmonization
optionB: Unified Profiles
optionC: Master Data Management
optionD: Data Marketplace
explanation:
For a customer with multiple disjointed data sources, the two most relevant Data Cloud functional areas are: (A) Data Harmonization — mapping disparate source data into a standardized data model so it can be used consistently; and (B) Unified Profiles — merging harmonized data across sources through identity resolution to create a single 360-degree customer view. Master Data Management (C) is a related discipline but not a specific Data Cloud capability. Data Marketplace (D) is for acquiring third-party data, not managing existing sources.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_data_cloud.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: A consultant is setting up a data stream with transactional data. Which field type should the consultant choose to ensure that leading zeros in the purchase order number are preserved?
optionA: Text
optionB: Number
optionC: Decimal
optionD: Serial
explanation:
Text fields store values as alphanumeric strings exactly as provided — including leading zeros. Number, Decimal, and Serial fields store values as numeric types and automatically strip leading zeros when parsing and storing the value. For a purchase order number like '00123', only a Text field preserves the '00' prefix. This is a key data modeling decision when ingesting identifiers that look numeric but must retain their full string representation.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_data_types.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: A retailer wants to unify profiles using Loyalty ID which is different than the unique ID of their customers. Which object should the consultant use in identity resolution to perform exact match rules on the Loyalty ID?
optionA: Party Identification object
optionB: Loyalty Identification object
optionC: Individual object
optionD: Contact Identification object
explanation:
The Party Identification DMO is the standard Data Cloud object for storing alternative or secondary identifiers for an individual — such as loyalty IDs, passport numbers, or any custom identifier that is distinct from the system primary key. By mapping the Loyalty ID to the Party Identification object and creating an exact match rule on that field, the consultant enables identity resolution to unify profiles based on shared loyalty IDs. There is no standard 'Loyalty Identification' or 'Contact Identification' object in Data Cloud (B, D). The Individual object (C) holds core identity attributes, not secondary IDs.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_match_rules.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_required_data_mappings.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: A Data Cloud Consultant is in the process of setting up data streams for a new service-based data source. When ingesting Case data, which field is recommended to be associated with the Event Time field?
optionA: Last Modified Date
optionB: Resolution Date
optionC: Escalation Date
optionD: Creation Date
explanation:
The Event Time field in Data Cloud represents when the event or record originated — for Case data, this is the Creation Date (the moment the case was opened). Event Time is used for time-based filtering in streaming insights and segmentation. Creation Date is the most semantically accurate choice for when the case 'happened.' Last Modified Date (A) represents when it was last changed, not when it occurred. Resolution Date (B) and Escalation Date (C) represent downstream states, not the originating event time.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_category.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: A consultant has an activation that is set to publish every 12 hours, but has discovered that updates to the data prior to activation are delayed by up to 24 hours. Which two areas should a consultant review to troubleshoot this issue? (Choose 2)
optionA: Review data transformations to ensure they're run after calculated insights
optionB: Review calculated insights to make sure they're run before segments are refreshed
optionC: Review segments to ensure they're refreshed after the data is ingested
optionD: Review calculated insights to make sure they're run after the segments are refreshed
explanation:
A 24-hour delay in data reaching activation suggests a pipeline sequencing issue. The two areas to check are: (B) Calculated insights must run before segments are refreshed — if insights run after segment refresh, the segment uses stale insight data; and (C) Segments must be refreshed after data ingestion completes — if the segment refresh runs before new data is ingested, it operates on the previous day's data. These two sequencing gaps together can create up to 24-hour delays. Data transformations run before calculated insights (A describes the wrong order). Calculated insights running after segment refresh (D) is the problem scenario, not the fix.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_insights.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_publish_segment.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: A consultant needs to minimize the difference between a Data Cloud segment population and Marketing Cloud data extension count to determine the true size of segments for campaign planning. What should the consultant recommend to filter the segments by to accomplish this?
optionA: Marketing Cloud Journeys
optionB: Business units
optionC: User preferences for marketing outreach
optionD: Geographical divisions
explanation:
The most common cause of a population difference between a Data Cloud segment and the resulting Marketing Cloud data extension count is that the segment contains unified individuals who belong to multiple Marketing Cloud business units. Filtering the segment by business unit ensures that only individuals with contact points in the relevant business unit are activated, aligning the counts. Journeys (A) affect who enters a campaign flow, not base segment size. User preferences (C) and geographical divisions (D) are criteria that could be applied but are not the standard answer to this specific population mismatch problem.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_segments.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_activation_for_a_segment.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: A customer has a calculated insight about lifetime value. What does the consultant need to be aware of if the calculated insight needs to be modified?
optionA: New dimensions can be added
optionB: Existing dimensions can be removed
optionC: Existing measures can be removed
optionD: New measures can be added
explanation:
The safe reading is that a calculated insight can be extended but not narrowed: new dimensions can be added to an existing insight (A), while removing an existing dimension (B) or an existing measure (C) is not available, because downstream segments and activations may already depend on them. Treat this item's option set with care, though — adding a new measure (D) is also possible, so A is not uniquely correct as printed, and the distinction the question is reaching for is between adding and removing rather than between dimensions and measures. If you are planning an insight that others will build on, the rule worth carrying is the one this item half-expresses: design the dimensions and measures you need up front, because you can extend the insight later but you cannot take pieces away.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_insights.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_calculated_insights_in_segments.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Cumulus Financial wants to create a segment of individuals based on transaction history data. This data has been mapped in the data model and is accessible via multiple container paths for segmentation. What happens if the optimal container path for this use case is not selected?
optionA: Alternate container paths will be suggested before the segment is published
optionB: The resulting segment may be smaller or larger than expected
optionC: Data Cloud segmentation will automatically select the optimal container path
optionD: The resulting segment will not be generated
explanation:
Container paths in segmentation determine how DMOs are joined when evaluating criteria. Different paths through the data model can yield different join cardinalities — the same logical criteria applied via different paths can produce different population counts (either over-counting or under-counting). Selecting the wrong path may result in a segment that is larger than expected (due to fan-out from a one-to-many join) or smaller (if the path excludes records). Data Cloud does not automatically suggest or select the optimal path (A, C). The segment will still generate — just with potentially incorrect membership (D is false).
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.c360_a_container_basics.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_considerations_for_related_attributes.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Which two requirements must be met for a calculated insight to appear in the segmentation canvas? (Choose 2)
optionA: The metrics of the calculated insights must only contain numeric values
optionB: The primary key of the segmented table must be a metric in the calculated insight
optionC: The calculated insight must contain a dimension including the Individual or Unified Individual Id
optionD: The primary key of the segmented table must be a dimension in the calculated insight
explanation:
For a calculated insight to appear in the segmentation canvas, two conditions must be met: (C) The insight must include a dimension that contains the Individual Id or Unified Individual Id — this links the insight back to the individual being segmented; and (D) The primary key of the table being segmented must appear as a dimension in the calculated insight — this allows Data Cloud to join the insight to the segmented entity. Metrics being numeric-only (A) is generally true but not the requirement for appearance in the canvas. The primary key being a metric (B) is incorrect — it must be a dimension.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_calculated_insights_in_segments.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: A company wants to include certain personalized fields in an email by including related attributes during the activation in Data Cloud. It notices that some values, such as purchased product names, do not have consistent casing in Marketing Cloud Engagement. The company wants to normalize all names to proper case and replace any null values with a default value. How should a consultant fulfill this requirement within Data Cloud?
optionA: Create a streaming insight with a data action
optionB: Use formula fields when ingesting at the data stream level
optionC: Create one batch data transform per data stream
optionD: Create one batch data transform that creates a new DLO
explanation:
A batch data transform that creates a new DLO is the correct approach for normalizing casing and replacing nulls across a dataset. The transform can apply PROPER() case functions and COALESCE/IFNULL logic across all records, writing the cleaned data to a new DLO that is then mapped and activated. Formula fields at ingestion (B) work on individual records at ingest time but are less suited for cross-record normalization and null replacement at scale. A streaming insight + data action (A) is for real-time event triggers, not batch data cleansing. One transform per data stream (C) is less efficient than a single transform that creates one consolidated DLO.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_batch_transform_formula.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Where is value suggestion for attributes in segmentation enabled when creating the DMO?
optionA: Data Mapping
optionB: Data Transformation
optionC: Segment Setup
optionD: Data Stream Setup
explanation:
Data Mapping is the right stage, because value suggestion is a property of the data model object rather than of any segment. Salesforce's page on the feature says you can enable value suggestions for DMO fields whose data type is Text, and that you enable or deactivate the feature in the DMO record home — the data-modeling area where the DMO is created and mapped — with a ceiling of 500 attributes across the org. The segment canvas is where the suggestions are consumed rather than switched on: you drag the attribute in and start typing in the Value field, and it can take up to 24 hours after modeling for values to appear. Data Transformation and Data Stream Setup both act on the data lake object before anything reaches the model. Note that no option names the DMO record home exactly, which is this item's wording weakness; Data Mapping is the option that describes the correct stage.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_suggested_values_in_segments.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: What should an organization use to stream inventory levels from an inventory management system into Data Cloud in a fast and scalable, near-real-time way?
optionA: Cloud Storage Connector
optionB: Commerce Cloud Connector
optionC: Ingestion API
optionD: Marketing Cloud Personalization Connector
explanation:
The Ingestion API is Data Cloud's mechanism for streaming data from external systems in near-real-time. It accepts JSON payloads via REST API calls, making it ideal for an inventory management system to push level changes as they occur — fast, scalable, and programmable. The Cloud Storage Connector (A) is for batch file-based ingestion, not real-time streaming. Commerce Cloud Connector (B) is specific to Salesforce B2C/B2B Commerce. Marketing Cloud Personalization Connector (D) is for behavioral personalization data, not inventory.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_data_ingestion.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Cumulus Financial wants its service agents to view a display of all cases associated with a Unified Individual on a contact record. Which two features should a consultant consider for this use case? (Choose 2)
optionA: Data Action
optionB: Profile API
optionC: Lightning Web Components
optionD: Query APL
explanation:
To surface unified Data Cloud profile data (including associated cases) directly on a Salesforce Contact record for service agents: (B) The Profile API allows querying unified individual data from Data Cloud programmatically; and (C) Lightning Web Components can be built to call the Profile API and display the results embedded on the Contact record page. Data Actions (A) trigger events from Data Cloud outward, not display data inward. Query APL (D) is Data Cloud's query language for analytics, not for embedding real-time data in Salesforce UI.

https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_data_cloud.htm&language=en_US&type=5
